investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable by the Kubernetes scheduler. The scheduler message is consistent across all three checks: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector, leaving zero viable scheduling targets and producing no evidence output whatsoever.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the 2 nodes that carry that resource label. The other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Because no node can accept the pod, the agent VM is never provisioned, and the eval runner never receives orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState — all four required evidence fields are missing. This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion or misconfiguration failure localized to the kata peer-pods scheduling layer, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable root cause, pod stuck for 144s, same 0/6 node breakdown.

failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was ever written, consistent with the pod never starting.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, confirming the agent VM was never provisioned.
source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) which requires a running VM pod before any evidence can be collected.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never scheduled.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=127356 — the check ran for ~127s before failing, consistent with the scheduler's 121s unscheduled timeout reported in the message.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote agent VMs or other peer-pod workloads have consumed all available VM slots on those nodes, leaving no capacity for new pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration: the pod spec targets only 2 nodes via affinity/selector rules, and those 2 nodes happen to be at capacity; if the selector is overly restrictive it may be excluding nodes that could otherwise host peer-pods.

Tertiary — peer-pods infrastructure scaling gap: the cluster may not have auto-scaled or added new kata-capable nodes in response to demand, resulting in a hard ceiling on concurrent remote agent VMs.

Quaternary — leaked or zombie VM allocations: previously created remote agent VMs that were not cleaned up may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, preventing new scheduling even when logical demand is low.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place new pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across all eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that the two nodes capable of hosting peer-pod VMs have no remaining VM slots, and preemption cannot free any slots. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no evidence of broader user-traffic or incident signals is present in the packet.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, meaning the effective schedulable pool is always just 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are at capacity for any reason, all remote-agent pods will be unschedulable.

The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1903) is intended to prevent this, but a prior crash or timeout could have bypassed cleanup.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable by the Kubernetes scheduler. The scheduler message is consistent across all three checks: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector, leaving zero viable scheduling targets and producing no evidence output whatsoever.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the 2 nodes that carry that resource label. The other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Because no node can accept the pod, the agent VM is never provisioned, and the eval runner never receives orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState — all four required evidence fields are missing. This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion or misconfiguration failure localized to the kata peer-pods scheduling layer, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 121s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable root cause, pod stuck for 144s, same 0/6 node breakdown.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable root cause, pod stuck for 146s, same 0/6 node breakdown.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was ever written, consistent with the pod never starting.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, confirming the agent VM was never provisioned.
source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) which requires a running VM pod before any evidence can be collected.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never scheduled.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=127356 — the check ran for ~127s before failing, consistent with the scheduler's 121s unscheduled timeout reported in the message.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote agent VMs or other peer-pod workloads have consumed all available VM slots on those nodes, leaving no capacity for new pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration: the pod spec targets only 2 nodes via affinity/selector rules, and those 2 nodes happen to be at capacity; if the selector is overly restrictive it may be excluding nodes that could otherwise host peer-pods.

Tertiary — peer-pods infrastructure scaling gap: the cluster may not have auto-scaled or added new kata-capable nodes in response to demand, resulting in a hard ceiling on concurrent remote agent VMs.

Quaternary — leaked or zombie VM allocations: previously created remote agent VMs that were not cleaned up may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, preventing new scheduling even when logical demand is low.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place new pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across all eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that the two nodes capable of hosting peer-pod VMs have no remaining VM slots, and preemption cannot free any slots. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no evidence of broader user-traffic or incident signals is present in the packet.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM onto any of the 6 available nodes — 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected against the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature in production-api has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every eval attempt that calls createAgent with type "remote" results in a pod stuck in Unschedulable state until the eval times out. This is a cluster-level resource constraint, not an eval infrastructure or code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:183-185: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false — all three failed with the same scheduler error, confirming the failure is at the VM provisioning layer, not the runtime response layer
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing peer-pod workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval-created agents. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity/selector, which may indicate a labeling change, node pool scaling event, or taint addition that reduced the schedulable node set from a previously larger pool.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning for peak eval load: the 2 kata-capable nodes may have insufficient total VM quota to absorb concurrent eval probes alongside production workloads, causing contention during the eval window.

Lower probability — a stuck or leaked peer-pod VM from a prior eval run that was not cleaned up (withCleanup path in run-status-probes.mjs) is holding a VM slot, artificially reducing available capacity.

reproductionSteps.details: All three should fail with the kata.peerpods.io/vm Unschedulable message if the cluster resource is still exhausted.

reproductionSteps.details: Use kubectl to describe the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and compare allocatable vs. requested quantities to confirm exhaustion.

reproductionSteps.label: List all running peer-pod VMs in the cluster namespace to identify any leaked or stuck pods
reproductionSteps.details: Check for pods in Pending, Running, or Terminating state that hold kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and were not cleaned up by a prior eval withCleanup path.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the 2 kata-capable nodes immediately using kubectl describe node to determine current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used counts and identify which workloads are holding VM slots.

Check for leaked or stuck eval pods in the cluster namespace that may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources without being cleaned up — cross-reference with the withCleanup path in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs.

If VM slots are confirmed exhausted by production workloads, assess whether the 2 kata-capable nodes can be scaled up (more VM quota) or whether additional kata-capable nodes can be added to the pool to restore eval scheduling headroom.
If the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes could support kata peer-pods with a label or taint change, evaluate whether expanding the schedulable node set is appropriate and safe for the production workload.

Re-run the three remote-agents eval checks after any remediation to confirm all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are returned and the message assertion ('hello from aura') passes.

This is an eval-layer failure with no user-traffic or incident signals in the supplied evidence; do not escalate as a user-facing outage unless kubectl inspection or incident signals confirm production remote agent provisioning is also failing for real users.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval probe to check if exhaustion is sustained
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion is ongoing or was transient at the time of the original run. A pass would indicate transient capacity pressure; a repeat Unschedulable failure confirms sustained exhaustion.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Describe kata-capable nodes to inspect VM resource allocatable vs. used
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms or refutes the VM slot exhaustion hypothesis and reveals how many slots are consumed vs. available.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Run kubectl describe node on each of the 2 nodes that carry kata.peerpods.io/vm and examine the Allocatable and Allocated Resources sections for that extended resource.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List all pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources in the relevant namespace
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether leaked eval pods from prior runs are consuming VM slots that should have been released by the withCleanup path in run-status-probes.mjs.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Run kubectl get pods --all-namespaces with resource field selectors or describe nodes to enumerate which workloads currently hold kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations, including any stuck eval pods.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect node affinity/selector on the remote agent pod spec
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes could ever be made eligible (e.g., by adding a label) or are intentionally excluded, and whether the selector is correct.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Retrieve the pod spec for a failing remote agent pod (kubectl get pod <pod-name> -o yaml) and compare its nodeSelector and affinity rules against the labels present on all 6 nodes.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agents sibling checks together
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms that all three checks share the same failure mode simultaneously, ruling out a sequencing or cleanup artifact where one eval's pod holds the last VM slot when the next eval runs.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the 2 kata-capable nodes shows available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling constraint (e.g., memory, CPU, or a quota policy) would need investigation.

If the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes are found to carry kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the pod's node selector is shown to be incorrect or stale, the primary cause would shift to a node labeling or affinity misconfiguration rather than resource exhaustion.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure window succeeds and produces all 5 required evidence fields, it would indicate a transient capacity spike rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.
If the eval runner's withCleanup path is shown to have successfully terminated all prior eval pods (no leaked peer-pod VMs), the leaked-VM hypothesis would be disproved.
If no kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is registered on any node in the cluster, the failure would indicate a cluster configuration regression rather than exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity across all nodes before attempting remote agent creation, and emit the counts as evidence fields — this would surface exhaustion before the pod scheduling timeout.

Add a cluster node inventory eval that verifies the expected number of kata-capable nodes are present and labeled correctly, catching node pool shrinkage or label drift before it affects agent scheduling.
Add a cleanup-verification eval step that confirms no orphaned remote-agent eval pods remain after each run, catching withCleanup failures that could leak VM slots across eval cycles.

Consider a shorter timeout or faster-failing sentinel for the remote-agent-create check so that VM exhaustion is detected and reported within the warningLatencyMs window (240000ms) rather than approaching the outageLatencyMs threshold (360000ms).
